title: console-navigation-ia-sketchpad-notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures an unstructured working draft of proposals and wireframe notes for a lightweight redesign of the Redwood Console navigation and information architecture (IA). The focus is on the left-hand sidebar, route hierarchy, and page-level composition so that product, eng, and design teams can align on a migration plan and initial backlog.

Objectives (why we are doing this):
- Reduce cognitive load for new users who try Redwood Console for the first time (trial users + engineers evaluating hosting vs private).
- Surface high-value operational flows (deploy, metrics, rollouts, logs, cost) in 2 clicks or fewer.
- Make per-customer and per-model contexts explicit and discoverable (context switch cost low).
- Create a routing and component pattern that supports host/dedicated/private feature flags and per-tenant entitlements.

Primary personas considered:
- Platform engineer: needs quick access to capacity, routing policies, and dedicated pool controls.
- Product engineer: launches models, views model performance dashboards, toggles rollouts, inspects traces.
- Solutions engineer / Customer success: inspects customer config, audit logs, and can impersonate a project.

Observed pain points (sourced from support tickets + internal interviews):
- Deeply nested menus for models and deployments — users lose track of where they are when jumping between models and projects (tickets: SPT-192, SPT-210).
- Overloaded top nav with feature toggles that are not discoverable to new users.
- Route URLs lack stable slugs for entities (model-version IDs are long numeric strings); links in docs break across rollouts.
- Sidebar currently mixes account-level settings and project-level operations without clear separation.

Design constraints and guardrails:
- Keep primary navigation compact to avoid scrolling on 1080p vertical layouts.
- Every primary nav item should map to a surface with < 3 deep click paths for critical flows.
- Backwards-compatible URL redirects for any old routes we remove.
- Feature flag gating: dedicated/private controls only visible based on entitlement.

Proposed top-level IA (flat primary nav):
- Home (dashboard): global overview, alerts, quick actions (create project, deploy model)
- Projects (global list + search): project-level switcher and create flow
- Models: canonical model catalog, versions, metrics, evals, quick deploy
- Deployments: live endpoints, runtimes, scaling, traffic split
- Observability: logs, traces, model latency heatmaps, per-route breakdown
- Cost & Quota: token spend, embedding units, forecast, reserved capacity usage
- Rollouts & Releases: canaries, A/B, policy, history
- Security & Compliance: audit logs, keys, SSO, SCIM
- Settings: account, billing, organization admin (moved out of top cluster)

Rationale for grouping:
- Projects is surfaced as a first-class object; much navigation will be 'Project -> Model -> Deployment'.
- Observability is consolidated to avoid users toggling between metrics, traces and logs in separate nav items.
- Rollouts deserves its own surface because users often have to coordinate releases across models and want history and rollback in one place.

Sidebar behavior and patterns:
- Collapsible left rail with two modes: compact icons-only and expanded (label + icon). Persist preference per-user in local storage and server-side user pref.
- Context header at top of sidebar shows current project (if set) and an overlay button to switch projects without leaving route. Clicking project header performs a soft context switch that updates the route prefix (/p/:projectId/...).
- Secondary nav introduced as an in-page horizontal subnav for model-specific pages (e.g., Overview | Versions | Metrics | Eval | Deploy).
- Active states should be deterministically derived from route patterns (see routing below) and not from local component state to avoid mismatch after refresh.

Routing patterns (stable, SEO-friendly, and bookmarkable):
- Global pages: /home, /projects, /models, /deployments, /observability, /cost, /rollouts, /security, /settings
- Project-scoped: /p/:projectSlug or /p/:projectSlug/models, /p/:projectSlug/models/:modelSlug, /p/:projectSlug/models/:modelSlug/versions/:versionSlug
- Deployment-scoped: /p/:projectSlug/deployments/:deploymentSlug or /deployments/:deploymentSlug (global lookup for cross-project views)
- Query params for ephemeral filters: ?env=staging&from=2026-02-01&to=2026-02-28
- Legacy redirects: /models/:numericId -> /models/:newSlug (server redirects and client-side hydration)

Wireframe notes (page-level):
- Model Overview (center column): name, description, quick deploy CTA, deployment health widget, recent evals, top 3 regressions. Right rail: recommended quantization / batching suggestions (from Optimize). Bottom: activity stream.
- Deployment Detail: header shows capacity, node pool, target latency, current rps. Primary CTA group (scale, restart, rollback). Lower: traffic split and per-region latency map.
- Observability Home: default time window = 1h, quick toggles to 24h/7d. Charts: request rate, p50/p95/p99, error rate, cost per 1k tokens. Ability to pin a chart to dashboard.

Backlog (initial grooming — prioritized):
1) IA-100: Implement project header and soft context switch (MVP) - acceptance: clicking project updates URL and top-of-page breadcrumb shows project. (owner: Jonah)
2) IA-110: Add Models top-level nav and migrate current model index page to /models - acceptance: old /models routes redirect to /models with 301. (owner: Rita)
3) IA-130: Sidebar compact / expanded state with server persisted pref - acceptance: preference survives sign out/in. (owner: Ethan)
4) IA-140: Implement route slugs and canonical redirect middleware - acceptance: old numeric ID links redirect; new slugs used in copyable share links. (owner: Platform eng)
5) IA-150: Observability consolidation (metrics + traces + logs) into single nav - acceptance: users can filter within page and pin to dashboards.
6) IA-160: Rollouts first-pass page with history and canary controls (design review needed)

Acceptance criteria notes for stories:
- All new primary nav items must be feature-flaggable and behind entitlements checks to avoid exposing Dedicated/private functionality.
- Unit and e2e tests for active-state calculation based on route pattern.
- Accessibility: keyboard-only nav, aria-expanded on sidebar sections, focus trap for context switcher modal.

Accessibility and internationalization considerations:
- Ensure contrast ratios for icon-only sidebar in compact mode.
- Allow top-level nav labels to be localized; ensure no hard-coded strings in routes.
- Screen reader: announce 'Project switched to X' when context switcher selects new project.

Migration plan and rollout approach:
- Phase 1 (MVP): implement Projects header, Models top-level, sidebar compact/expanded (behind ff 'ia_v1'). Deploy to staging and enable for 10% of accounts. Monitor drop-offs in navigation usage and capture user sessions.
- Phase 2: slugs and redirects, observability consolidation, rollout page MVP. Enable for 50% and iterate on telemetry.
- Phase 3: full rollout and cleanup of legacy routes + docs. Migrate help articles and update public docs site with new canonical URLs.

Telemetry & metrics to watch during rollout:
- Time to first meaningful action (create model or deploy) from signup landing.
- Number of context switches per session.
- Drop-off rate when navigating from Models -> Deployments.
- Support tickets referencing "can't find X" for top-level nav items (tagging rule).

Open questions / items for design/eng sync:
- Should Projects be the default landing page for enterprise accounts or Home dashboard? (we should A/B test)
- Do we want a quick search (global command palette) vs larger Projects list for power users? Implementation trade-offs.
- How to handle cross-project deployments in naming and routes? single deployments page with project filter or always project-scoped?
- How to expose per-route rate limiting controls without cluttering Deployments page? Proposed: collapsible advanced section.

Next steps (short-term):
- Schedule design session to produce 3 annotated wireframes for Model Overview, Deployment Detail, and Observability consolidation (owner: Rita). Due: 2026-03-10.
- Platform to prototype slug redirects and route middleware (owner: Ethan). Draft RFC by 2026-03-05.
- Product to finalize prioritization and scope IA-100..IA-140 for Q2 planning (owner: Maya).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a sketchpad doc; expect iterative changes. Add inline comments or link to the Confluence IA epic for more formal specs. Prefer short, actionable feedback (e.g., "move X to top nav" vs long essays).

Recent discussion links and references:
- Slack thread: #product-console "nav-redesign" (search thread id above)
- JIRA epic: JIRA-IAEPIC-78 (contains wireframes and acceptance criteria)
- Confluence: Console IA goals (linked in linked_artifacts)

End of sketchpad.
